_comment: Trips shown on the 'pick a trip' map of the Japan page. Each trip is a start town, end town and fork picks on the page; `top` is the rank from the guides (1-15). `geo` and `networks` are written by tools/trips_geo.py from the published page - never by hand.

trips.name: Cape to cape
trips.note: The whole country, north to south · Sea of Japan coast, Noto, Biwa, the Inland Sea, Kyushu

trips.name: Shimanami Kaidō
trips.note: National cycle route · seven bridges across the Seto Inland Sea on their own bike lanes · 70 km
trips.why: Japan's most famous ride, on every list first: island-hopping over the bridges with the blue line all the way

trips.name: Biwaichi
trips.note: National cycle route round Lake Biwa, Japan's largest lake · anticlockwise: the north tip, Nagahama, Hikone castle, Ōtsu, then the west shore back · flat, the blue line all the way
trips.why: the classic weekend loop from Kyoto: 190 km of lakeside on quiet roads and paths, with a castle town and hot springs on the way

trips.name: Noto Peninsula
trips.note: Ishikawa Satoyama-Satoumi national route · Nanao, Suzu, Wajima, the Senmaida rice terraces, the Chirihama beach drive · check the road state after the 2024 earthquake
trips.why: the Sea of Japan at its wildest: fishing villages, terraced fields and an 8 km beach you ride on the sand

trips.name: Ring-Ring Road
trips.note: Tsukuba–Kasumigaura national route · the old railway path to Tsuchiura, then round Lake Kasumigaura: north shore, the Tamatsukuri road station, Asō, Itako, back along the south shore · flat all the way
trips.why: the flattest famous ride in Japan and the nearest to Tokyo: a rail trail and a lake loop with hardly a climb, good for a first day on the bike

trips.name: Fuji-ichi
trips.note: National cycle route round Mt Fuji (163 km signed; our line 130 km) · Lake Yamanaka, Gotemba, the south foot to Fujinomiya, the Asagiri plateau, Lake Motosu and the western lakes back to Kawaguchiko
trips.why: the mountain in view the whole way round: five lakes, high plateaus, two real climbs

trips.name: Toyama Bay
trips.note: National cycle route Himi ↔ Asahi, 102 km · the Tateyama mountains across the water, Amaharashi coast, Toyama and Takaoka
trips.why: the 3,000 m Tateyama range seen straight across the sea from a flat coast road

trips.name: Tokapuchi 400
trips.note: National cycle route round the Tokachi plain, 403 km signed; our loop 338 km · north through Kamishihoro and Ashoro to Ikeda, then the Pacific coast: Urahoro, Hiroo, back up through Nakasatsunai · grassland, dairy farms, straight empty roads · get to Obihiro by the Sapporo leg or the train
trips.why: Hokkaidō's big-sky ride: the widest farmland in Japan, almost no traffic, the mountains on the horizon all the way round

trips.name: Awa-ichi
trips.note: round Awaji Island: the east coast to Sumoto, the southern cliffs past Yura and Monzaki to Fukura and the Naruto whirlpools, back up the west coast past Goshiki · get there by the Jenova Line ferry from Akashi (13 min, bikes welcome) · the Naruto bridge has no bike path, so it is a loop, not a way into Shikoku
trips.why: the Inland Sea's island loop: 150 km of coast road, onsen towns and the whirlpools, an easy weekend from Kobe or Osaka

trips.name: Yamanami Highway
trips.note: Beppu's hot springs, up to Yufuin, the Kujū highlands over the Makinoto pass (1,330 m), down into the Aso caldera · 97 km, 2,000 m of climbing · continue via Takachiho gorge to the coast at Nobeoka
trips.why: the classic Kyushu climb: volcanic grassland, hot-spring villages and a caldera view from the top

trips.name: Pacific Cycling Road
trips.note: National cycle route Chōshi → Taiji, 1,400 km, Japan's longest · Kujūkuri beach, the Bōsō coast, the Tokyo Bay ferry to Kurihama, Kamakura, Fuji from the coast, Ise, the Kii peninsula · blue arrows most of the way
trips.why: the long one: the whole Pacific side from Chōshi round the Kii peninsula, with the Tokyo Bay ferry in the middle

trips.name: Tobishima Kaidō
trips.note: ferry Imabari → Okamura, then seven bridges through the quiet Tobishima islands to Kure · citrus groves, the old port of Mitarai
trips.why: the Shimanami's quiet sister: the same island bridges with almost no traffic

trips.name: Keinawa
trips.note: Kyoto, the Kizu river path to Nara, Asuka and the old capitals, Gojō, the Kinokawa valley to Wakayama · the signed Keinawa cycle route, three prefectures · rejoins the Pacific line at Wakayama
trips.why: river paths and temples: the quiet way from Kyoto to the sea through Japan's oldest capitals

trips.name: Nichinan Coast
trips.note: Aoshima, Udo shrine in the cliffs, Cape Toi and its wild horses · palms and Pacific surf · 75 km
trips.why: Kyushu's sunny southern coast: cliff shrines, palm trees and a warm sea

trips.name: Kibi Plain
trips.note: the Kibiji cycle path · Kibitsu shrine, burial mounds, the Bitchū Kokubunji pagoda in the rice fields · 19 km, flat
trips.why: the classic easy half-day: a car-free path through the old Kibi kingdom's shrines and tombs

trips.name: Tottori Uminami Road
trips.note: National cycle route Iwami → Sakaiminato, 152 km · the Tottori sand dunes, the San'in Kaigan geopark coast, Daisen behind
trips.why: sand dunes, sea caves and the geopark coast on the quiet side of Honshu

trips.name: Fukushima Hamadōri
trips.note: National cycle route Shinchi → Iwaki, 179 km · the recovering coast north of Iwaki

trips.name: Amaichi
trips.note: National cycle route (Kyushu's first, July 2026) Misumi → Ushibuka, 152 km · the Amakusa Five Bridges, the Ariake and Yatsushiro seas, Hondo, Tomioka castle, the hidden-Christian churches at Ōe and Sakitsu (World Heritage), Ushibuka port · reached from Aso over Kumamoto

trips.name: Okhotsk Cycling Road
trips.note: the old Yūmō railway line along the Sea of Okhotsk: Lake Saroma, Yūbetsu, Monbetsu · flat, remote, drift ice in winter · reached from the Tokachi loop over Ashoro and Kitami

trips.name: Yūyake Kōyō Line
trips.note: Route 378 along Ehime's west coast: Iyo, Futami, Nagahama, Yawatahama, then Mikame and the Uwakai bays to Uwajima · mikan orchards, sunsets over the Inland Sea, one real climb in the middle

trips.name: Bōsō coast and Tokyo Bay
trips.note: the Ōarai seaside, Chōshi, Kujūkuri beach, Katsuura, Tateyama, the Tokyo Bay ferry Kanaya → Kurihama · the coast way round Tokyo instead of through it

trips.name: Lake Hamana
trips.note: the Hamanako cycling road round the lake · flat · a family ride in the guides

trips.name: Sanriku to Matsushima
trips.note: the Sanriku recovery road down to Matsushima Bay, one of Japan's three great views

trips.name: Hokkaidō west coast
trips.note: the empty northern coast, Otaru, the Yōtei line through Niseko country

trips.name: Sapporo to Tokachi
trips.note: Iwamizawa, Ashibetsu, the Furano lavender valley, the Karikachi pass (644 m) on Route 38, Shintoku · the way east from the crossing; Route 274 over Nissho is closed at Hobetsu

trips.name: Tokachi to the Okhotsk sea
trips.note: Kamishihoro, Ashoro, over the hills to Kitami, Abashiri and the Okhotsk coast to Monbetsu

trips.name: Tōhoku Pacific
trips.note: Hachinohe, the Sanriku rias coast, Kesennuma, Matsushima

trips.name: Kyoto to Hiroshima
trips.note: Osaka, Himeji castle, the Kibi plain, Shimanami and Tobishima bridges, Kure

trips.name: Kyushu east coast
trips.note: the Kunisaki peninsula, Beppu, the Nichinan coast, Cape Sata · or turn inland at Beppu over the Yamanami Highway and Aso
